$comment: The council. Every entry was verified by running it — command, flags, and a live round-trip.
Latencies are a FLOOR measured on a one-word answer. A real question is minutes.
Every member runs READ-ONLY and from a scratch directory outside your repo. They advise;
they never edit. Context is ASSEMBLED and passed in, never granted — read-only in these
CLIs means 'cannot write', not 'cannot read', so a member with repo access could read your
.env and your credentials.
No API keys. Every member is a CLI you already have logged in.
── promptVia: how the prompt reaches this member, and why it is per-member ──
stdin  written to the child's stdin. The args must NOT contain {prompt}.
file    written to a 0600 file in the scratch dir; {promptFile} is substituted.
argv    substituted into {prompt}. Size-checked against the platform limit and REFUSED
rather than allowed to die as E2BIG mid-run.
argv used to be the only path, and it was wrong two ways — both measured 2026-07-28:
Linux caps a single argv string at 131,072 bytes (160,000 → E2BIG), which is BELOW this
project's own 160,000-char context budget; and /proc/<pid>/cmdline is mode 444, so the whole
assembled pack was readable by every user on the box for the duration of the call.
Do not change a promptVia without re-running `--verify-delivery`. A wrong value does not
error: `agy` given a prompt on stdin exits 0 and answers 'How can I help you today?' because
the prompt never arrived — a fluent answer to an empty question, which then gets ranked.
── family: declared, not guessed ──
The family-mix diagnostic used to infer the vendor from the member id, with 'Google' as the
fallback — so every member of a custom roster not named exactly `codex` or `grok` was
reported as Google. Declare it.
Override this file by creating .council/members.json in your own project.
── readOnlyBy: the flags that actually deliver the read-only guarantee ──
The test used to assert read-only by pattern-matching the args for /read-only|plan|--print|-p$/.
That passed for the wrong reason (grok matched on a bare `-p`) and then broke the moment grok
moved to --prompt-file, even though nothing about its permissions had changed. A regex over
flags cannot tell a permission from a coincidence.
So each member NAMES the flags that constrain it, and the test asserts those exact tokens are
still present in args. A declaration alone would be self-certifying; this one is checkable.
-- contained: measured, never assumed --
`contained` is written ONLY by scripts/verify-containment.mjs having demonstrated that the member
cannot write - a cwd probe and an absolute-path escape probe. Do not hand-edit it to true.
council.mjs EXCLUDES an uncontained member by default. A four-member council that keeps the
package's promise is worth more than a five-member one that quietly breaks it.
-- {timeoutMin}: a member CLI must not out-wait, or under-wait, the council --
agy self-aborts after --print-timeout (default 5m). Pinning it to a literal 14m was right for the
default --timeout of 15 and silently wrong for every other value: --timeout=30 left a member that
still quit at 14 minutes and was reported as a plain failure. {timeoutMin} is substituted from the
run’s actual --timeout, one minute under it, so the two cannot drift.

Reasoning effort pinned per skills/pick-the-model. --skip-git-repo-check is required because the scratch dir is deliberately not a repo — it relaxes a git check, NOT the sandbox, which stays read-only. members.label: Grok 4.5
members.verified: 2026-07-28, 14s floor; --prompt-file round-trip verified with a canary
members.note: Only grok-4.5 is offered on this account. Web search off so the council reasons rather than retrieves. --prompt-file is better than stdin here: no pipe, no argv, and the file is 0600 in the scratch dir and removed the moment the member exits. NOT CONTAINED. Measured 2026-07-28 by scripts/verify-containment.mjs: grok writes a file into its cwd AND to an arbitrary absolute path outside it. --permission-mode plan, --sandbox read-only, --tools <allowlist> and --disallowed-tools are all accepted without complaint and NONE of them stop it. It was previously listed as read-only because the roster test matched a bare `-p`, which is a prompt flag, not a permission. Excluded from the council by default; --allow-uncontained opts back in, and the run says so in its output and in the run file.

members.label: Gemini 3.1 Pro (Antigravity)
members.note: Reached via Antigravity (agy 1.1.8), NOT the gemini CLI — that one now refuses this account outright: 'no longer supported for Gemini Code Assist for individuals'. gemini-3.1-pro-high is the highest 3.1 tier offered; there is no -max. THE ONLY argv-ONLY MEMBER: `agy` has no stdin path and no --prompt-file, and piping to it silently answers an empty prompt. So it is the one member that can be refused for prompt size on Linux, and the one whose prompt is visible in the process table. --print-timeout is substituted from --timeout ({timeoutMin}m) because it DEFAULTS TO 5m — under our 15m member timeout, so on a large context it would abort itself and be reported as a failure with no indication why.
